newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's new president sacks army chief.
newsitem.headline: Albania's new president sacks army chief.

text.p: Albanian President Rexhep Meidani has sacked the army's chief of staff in a bid to rid the Balkan country's armed forces of the old guard, the president's office said on Tuesday.

Adem Copani, promoted by former president Sali Berisha to the top post in March when widespread protests and a wave of violence ripped through Europe's most impoverished state, has been replaced by 46-year-old Aleks Andoni.
Berisha and his Democratic Party government were forced to resign for failing to check the spread of shady investment funds whose collapse ignited an armed uprising.
A Socialist-led coalition swept to power in June elections and has vowed to start rebuilding the ravaged country by reforming the police, the army and the financial system.
The defence ministry called this month for the resignation of the top 25 army generals for conceiving and carrying out attacks on civilians in southern Albania, scene of the worst bloodshed.
Copani was not publicly named, but denied any part in the attacks in a newspaper interview. He insisted the head of the secret police took command when a state of emergency was imposed in March.
Defence Minister Sabit Brokaj told parliament last week he would dismiss "inexperienced and incriminated" people from the army and replace them with experienced officers.
A NATO delegation is currently in the capital Tirana to assist with the restructuring of the armed forces.
